items.name: b12754
items.body:
<details open>

ggml-openvino: fix CI op tests and improve KV cache decode (#33002)

* ggml-openvino: write back consumed in-place nodes of op-test graphs

On the naive path every node of an op-test graph is a model output,
except an in-place node that another node reads: it got no output, so
its destination buffer was never written. GATED_DELTA_NET_CACHE_FUSION
copies the final state into the cache and then reads the copy, so the
cache kept its old contents.

Write such a node back through its view_src, as is already done when
nothing reads it. Model graphs are unchanged.

* ggml-openvino: keep the rest of the buffer in a partial in-place FILL

An in-place FILL on a view into part of a larger buffer produced only
the filled values. Its output stands for the whole in-place source, so
the write-back put those values at the start of the buffer and not at
the view's offset.

For a contiguous view with a static shape, build the whole buffer: the
elements before the view, the filled values, then the elements after
it. Add NodeContext::get_inplace_op_src() to detect the in-place case.

* ggml-openvino: fix softplus precision for large negative inputs

softplus was computed as relu(x) + log(1 + exp(-|x|)). When exp(-|x|)
is below the precision of 1 + exp(-|x|), the log returns 0 or one ulp,
so for x below about -16 in f32 the result was 0 or far off. The
SOFTPLUS test case with inputs in [-16.6, -16] fails on CPU and GPU.

Compute log1p(y) for y = exp(-|x|) with the series
y - y^2/2 + y^3/3 - y^4/4 when y < 0.01, where its relative error is
below 2e-9, and keep log(1 + y) above that.

* ggml-openvino: finer GPU KV rounding for decode batches

Rounding the GPU KV length up to a power of two makes a batch attend up
to twice the rows that hold data right after each power of two.

items.body:
<details open>

server : handle CTRL_BREAK_EVENT on Windows for clean shutdown (#32080)

Windows can't send SIGINT to a child process, so scripts that launch
llama-server could only kill it, which skips the clean shutdown. The
console control handler only handled CTRL_C_EVENT, so a CTRL_BREAK_EVENT
sent to the server's own process group ended it with
STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT.

- server: handle CTRL_BREAK_EVENT the same as CTRL_C_EVENT in the
  console control handler
- scripts/moe-cache-tune.py: on Windows, start the server in a new
  process group and stop it with CTRL_BREAK_EVENT. On other platforms,
  stop it with SIGINT. In both cases, kill it afterwards as a fallback.
- tests: add test_server_ctrl_break (Windows only) and a
  ServerProcess.share_console option. Console control events only
  reach a server that shares the test's console, hence the option.

</details>
